---
title: Keep a copy in sync
description: Follow an instance's event stream from a cursor, so a copy of your data stays current and picks up where it stopped after a break.
---

A search index, a cache or a report keeps its own copy of an instance's data. Read what you need once, then apply each change from the [event stream](/events) and save a cursor, so that after a break you receive everything you missed and nothing twice. The [Swift SDK](/swift-sdk) and the [CLI](/cli) do this for you.

You need a credential that can read the types you copy. A copy that answers reads offline in the instance's place, as a device does, needs [more](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/reach.md).

## What the stream sends

Both clients read the same stream, and each shows it in its own form. From cursor `4`, narrowed to notes, `marfa events` prints one frame a line:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa events --type core.note --edges none --from 4
```

```text
-  stream_cursor  6
6  item.created  01a15f3c-db7b-745c-a178-be82b8caa2a0
-  stream_live  6
```

</Terminal>

Over HTTP, the [stream](/api-reference/event-stream/streamEvents) takes your cursor in the `Last-Event-ID` header and answers server-sent events. This is the same stream, with the item cut short:

```http title="Request"
GET /events?type=core.note&edges=none
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Last-Event-ID: 4
```

```sse title="Response" status="200" note="Server-sent events"
: connected

event: stream_cursor
data: {"event_type":"stream_cursor","cursor":"6"}

id: 6
event: item.created
data: {"event_type":"item.created","item":{"id":"01a15f3c-db7b-745c-a178-be82b8caa2a0","type":"core.note",...},"metadata":{...}}

event: stream_live
data: {"event_type":"stream_live","cursor":"6"}
```

In both, the stream opens with `stream_cursor`, which names the **head of the log**, the latest event. It replays every event after your cursor, sends `stream_live` when it has caught up, then sends each new event as it happens. Event 5 changed a task, so the filter left it out and the IDs skip it.

Only events carry an `id:` line, so **the last `id:` you received is always a cursor you can resume from**. Lines that start with `:` are comments: Marfa sends `:ping` every 30 seconds while the stream is quiet. The Catalog's [Events](/catalog/events) page lists every event and its fields.

## Build the sync

`sync.ts` keeps a copy of every note in a JSON file. On its first run, it takes the head of the log, reads the notes, then follows the stream from that head. Because it takes the head first, every change made while it reads waits in the log.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Read the frames

A browser `EventSource` can't send an `Authorization` header, and the TypeScript SDK doesn't read streams, so read the stream with `fetch`:

```ts title="sync.ts"
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createClient, pages, type components } from "@withmarfa/client";

const baseUrl = process.env.MARFA_API_URL!;
const credential = process.env.MARFA_API_KEY!;
const marfa = createClient({ baseUrl, credential });

type Frame = { id?: string; event: string; data: string };

async function* readFrames(body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>>): AsyncGenerator<Frame> {
  let buffer = "";
  for await (const text of body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream())) {
    buffer += text;
    const blocks = buffer.split("\n\n");
    buffer = blocks.pop() ?? "";
    for (const block of blocks) {
      const frame: Frame = { event: "message", data: "" };
      for (const line of block.split("\n")) {
        if (line.startsWith(":")) continue; // a comment, such as the ping
        const colon = line.indexOf(":");
        const field = colon === -1 ? line : line.slice(0, colon);
        const value = colon === -1 ? "" : line.slice(colon + 1).replace(/^ /, "");
        if (field === "id") frame.id = value;
        else if (field === "event") frame.event = value;
        else if (field === "data") frame.data += (frame.data ? "\n" : "") + value;
      }
      if (frame.data !== "") yield frame;
    }
  }
}

async function open(cursor?: string): Promise<ReadableStream<Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>>> {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/events?type=core.note&edges=none`, {
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${credential}`,
      ...(cursor === undefined ? {} : { "Last-Event-ID": cursor }),
    },
  });
  if (!response.ok || response.body === null) {
    throw new Error(`The stream answered ${response.status}`);
  }
  return response.body;
}
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Keep the copy and its cursor together

Save the cursor **in the same place as the copy, in step with what you apply**: here, one file written after each event. An item event carries the item as it stands after the change, so `apply` replaces what the copy holds, or removes it for `item.purged`. An event the copy already reflects changes nothing.

```ts title="sync.ts"
type Item = components["schemas"]["Item"];
type Copy = { cursor?: string; notes: Record<string, Item> };
const file = "notes-copy.json";
let copy: Copy = await readFile(file, "utf8").then(JSON.parse, () => ({ notes: {} }));

function apply(event: { event_type: string; item: Item }) {
  if (event.event_type === "item.purged") delete copy.notes[event.item.id];
  else copy.notes[event.item.id] = event.item;
}

async function saveCursor(cursor: string) {
  copy.cursor = cursor;
  await writeFile(file, JSON.stringify(copy));
}
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Follow the stream

`follow` applies each event and saves its ID. It returns the frame that ended the stream, or `closed` if the connection dropped.

```ts title="sync.ts"
async function follow(cursor: string): Promise<string> {
  for await (const frame of readFrames(await open(cursor))) {
    const data = JSON.parse(frame.data);
    switch (frame.event) {
      case "stream_cursor":
        break;
      case "stream_live":
        if (data.cursor !== null) await saveCursor(data.cursor);
        break;
      case "stream_incomplete":
      case "catchup_too_old":
      case "cursor_ahead":
        return frame.event;
      default:
        apply(data);
        await saveCursor(frame.id!);
    }
  }
  return "closed";
}
```

Save the `cursor` of `stream_live` too: on a narrow stream, the last event can be far behind the head. Marfa sends each event after your cursor exactly once, even across a server restart.

</Step>
<Step>

### Start from the head of the log

`rebuild` takes the head from the first frame, lists every note in every state with the [TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk), and saves the head as the cursor. The listing and the stream both ask for notes and no edges, so the copy holds exactly what the stream keeps current.

```ts title="sync.ts"
async function rebuild(): Promise<string> {
  let head: string | undefined;
  for await (const frame of readFrames(await open())) {
    if (frame.event === "stream_cursor") head = JSON.parse(frame.data).cursor;
    break; // closes the stream
  }
  if (head === undefined) throw new Error("The stream didn't name the head of the log");
  copy = { notes: {} };
  const notes = pages(async (cursor) => {
    const { data, error } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
      params: { query: { type: "core.note", state: "any", cursor } },
    });
    if (error) throw new Error(error.error.message);
    return data;
  });
  for await (const item of notes) apply({ event_type: "item.created", item: item as Item });
  await saveCursor(head);
  return head;
}
```

When Marfa can't read the head in time, the first frame is `stream_live` with a `null` cursor, so `rebuild` throws.

</Step>
<Step>

### Run it

The loop resumes from the saved cursor after a break, and rebuilds when the cursor can't be used:

```ts title="sync.ts"
let cursor = copy.cursor; // undefined on the first run
for (;;) {
  cursor ??= await rebuild();
  const ended = await follow(cursor);
  cursor = ended === "catchup_too_old" || ended === "cursor_ahead" ? undefined : copy.cursor;
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
}
```

Run it as an ES module, with `MARFA_API_URL` and `MARFA_API_KEY` set.

</Step>
</Steps>

## When the stream ends

What ends a stream tells you what to do:

| You see | It means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The connection closes with no frame | A network or proxy fault. | Wait a moment, then resume from your saved cursor. |
| `stream_incomplete` | The stream couldn't go on, for the `reason` it names, such as `server_stopping`. Everything after your cursor is still in the log. | Resume from your saved cursor. For `credential_ended`, use a key that's valid. For `reader_behind`, take frames off the connection as they arrive and apply them from a queue. |
| `catchup_too_old` | The log no longer holds the events after your cursor. By default it keeps them for at least 30 days. | Rebuild from the head of the log. |
| `cursor_ahead` | Your cursor is past the log's head, as after the instance was restored from a backup. | Discard the cursor and rebuild from the head of the log. |

`marfa events` exits `1` for `cursor_ahead` and `catchup_too_old`, `3` for a `stream_incomplete` that a new stream can mend, and `5` for `credential_ended`, so a script needn't read the frames. [Exit codes](/cli#exit-codes) lists every status.

A stream can also be refused before it opens, and then `open` throws:

- **`429 rate_limited`:** wait the seconds `Retry-After` names, then try again.
- **`503 stream_capacity_exhausted`:** the instance is serving as many streams as it allows. Try again later.
- **Anything else,** such as `403 type_not_permitted`, `400 unknown_type`, or `400 validation_error` for a cursor the stream didn't write, is a fault in the credential or the request. Fix it rather than retry.

[Stream change events](/api-reference/event-stream/streamEvents) lists every answer.

## Narrow the stream

`type` limits item events to a type and its subtypes. It takes up to ten types or patterns, separated by commas, such as `core.note,app.*`. Edge events come whatever `type` says, so send `edges=none` to leave them out, as `sync.ts` does.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa events --type core.note --type core.task --edges none --from 4
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /events?type=core.note,core.task&edges=none
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Last-Event-ID: 4
```

A cursor works under any filter, so you can change the filter between connections.

The rules behind this guide are in the [events](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md) chapter of the contract.
